scientific_name: Mandevilla x amabilis 'Sun Parasol Giant Pink'

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed when soil and air are warm; in zone 9 plant March-May. Sun Parasol Giant Pink is a large-flowered selection from the Sun Parasol mandevilla series bred for outdoor performance in warm climates. The plant twines naturally and needs a trellis, fence, pergola, or other structure to climb.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil. Sun Parasol Giant Pink bears exceptionally large, funnel-shaped flowers in a vivid rose-pink, noticeably bigger than many other mandevilla cultivars, opening continuously from late spring through frost on a vigorous twining vine. Its oversized blooms and glossy dark green foliage make it a dramatic choice for covering a trellis, pergola, or fence with tropical color through the heat of a Gulf South summer, and the trumpet-shaped flowers attract hummingbirds reliably. In the warmest zone 9 locations the plant may survive mild winters as a semi-woody perennial; in most of zone 9 treat as an annual or move container-grown plants indoors before frost. The milky sap is irritating to some people, so wear gloves when pruning.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Mandevilla Vines for Florida

Sun Parasol Apricot is a warm-toned selection from the Sun Parasol mandevilla series bred for outdoor performance in warm climates. The plant twines naturally and needs a trellis, fence, pergola, or other structure to climb.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil. Sun Parasol Apricot bears large, funnel-shaped flowers in a warm, blended apricot-orange with a deeper throat, a less common color among mandevilla cultivars that pairs well with tropical foliage plants and warm-toned companions on a sunny patio. It blooms continuously from late spring through frost on a vigorous twining vine that quickly covers a trellis, pergola, or fence, and the trumpet-shaped flowers attract hummingbirds reliably. In the warmest zone 9 locations the plant may survive mild winters as a semi-woody perennial; in most of zone 9 treat as an annual or move container-grown plants indoors before frost. The milky sap is irritating to some people, so wear gloves when pruning.
